“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ yuganandhaṃ (ka. sī. aṭṭha.) bhāveti. Tassa samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ [V 0.0274] bhāvayato maggo sañjāyati. So taṃ maggaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tassa taṃ maggaṃ āsevato bhāvayato [P 2.0093] bahulīkaroto saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.

“Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu develops serenity and insight yoked together. As he is developing serenity and insight yoked together, the path is generated. He cultivates, develops, and makes much of that path. For one who cultivates, develops, and makes much of that path, the fetters are abandoned and the underlying tendencies are brought to an end.

“Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhuno dhammuddhaccaviggahitaṃ mānasaṃ hoti. So, āvuso, samayo yaṃ taṃ cittaṃ ajjhattameva ajjhattaññeva (syā. ka.) santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi [M 0.0284] hoti samādhiyati. Tassa maggo sañjāyati. So taṃ maggaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti. Tassa taṃ maggaṃ āsevato bhāvayato bahulīkaroto saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.

“Furthermore, friends, a bhikkhu’s mind is seized by agitation about phenomena. There comes an occasion, friends, when his mind becomes internally steady, settles down, becomes unified, and is concentrated. The path is generated for him. He cultivates, develops, and makes much of that path. For one who cultivates, develops, and makes much of that path, the fetters are abandoned and the underlying tendencies are brought to an end.

“Yo hi koci, āvuso, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā mama santike arahattapattaṃ byākaroti, sabbaso imehi catūhi maggehi, etesaṃ vā aññatarenā”ti.

“Friends, any bhikkhu or bhikkhunī who declares the attainment of arahantship in my presence does so entirely by these four paths, or by one of them.”

1. Suttantaniddeso

1. Exposition of the Discourse

2. Kathaṃ samathapubbaṅgamaṃ vipassanaṃ bhāveti? Nekkhammavasena cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi. Tattha jāte dhamme aniccato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā, dukkhato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā, anattato [T 1.0434] anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā. Iti paṭhamaṃ samatho, pacchā vipassanā. Tena vuccati – “samathapubbaṅgamaṃ vipassanaṃ bhāvetī”ti. Bhāvetīti catasso bhāvanā – tattha jātānaṃ dhammānaṃ anativattanaṭṭhena bhāvanā, indriyānaṃ ekarasaṭṭhena bhāvanā, tadupagavīriyavāhanaṭṭhena bhāvanā, āsevanaṭṭhena bhāvanā.

2. How does one develop insight preceded by serenity? By way of renunciation, one-pointedness of mind and non-distraction is concentration. Therein, insight is in the sense of contemplating arisen phenomena as impermanent; insight is in the sense of contemplating them as suffering; insight is in the sense of contemplating them as nonself. Thus, serenity is first, insight afterwards. Therefore it is said: ‘one develops insight preceded by serenity.’ ‘Develops’ means four kinds of development: development in the sense of not overstepping the phenomena that have arisen therein; development in the sense of the faculties having a single function; development in the sense of conveying the energy appropriate to that; and development in the sense of cultivation.

Maggo sañjāyatīti kathaṃ maggo sañjāyati? Dassanaṭṭhena sammādiṭṭhi maggo sañjāyati, abhiniropanaṭṭhena sammāsaṅkappo maggo sañjāyati, pariggahaṭṭhena sammāvācā maggo sañjāyati, samuṭṭhānaṭṭhena sammākammanto maggo sañjāyati, vodānaṭṭhena sammāājīvo maggo sañjāyati, paggahaṭṭhena sammāvāyāmo maggo sañjāyati, upaṭṭhānaṭṭhena sammāsati maggo sañjāyati, avikkhepaṭṭhena sammāsamādhi maggo sañjāyati – evaṃ maggo sañjāyati.

‘The path is known’—how is the path known? In the sense of seeing, right view is known as the path. In the sense of applying the mind, right intention is known as the path. In the sense of encompassing, right speech is known as the path. In the sense of originating, right action is known as the path. In the sense of cleansing, right livelihood is known as the path. In the sense of exerting, right effort is known as the path. In the sense of establishing, right mindfulness is known as the path. In the sense of non-distraction, right concentration is known as the path. It is in this way that the path is known.

So taṃ maggaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti āsevatīti kathaṃ āsevati? Āvajjanto āsevati, jānanto āsevati, passanto āsevati, paccavekkhanto āsevati, cittaṃ [P 2.0094] adhiṭṭhahanto āsevati, saddhāya adhimuccanto āsevati, vīriyaṃ paggaṇhanto āsevati, satiṃ upaṭṭhāpento āsevati, cittaṃ samādahanto āsevati, paññāya pajānanto āsevati, abhiññeyyaṃ [V 0.0275] abhijānanto āsevati, pariññeyyaṃ parijānanto āsevati, pahātabbaṃ pajahanto āsevati[M 0.0285], bhāvetabbaṃ [T 1.0435] bhāvento āsevati, sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikaronto āsevati – evaṃ āsevati.

He cultivates, develops, and makes much of that path. Herein, how does one cultivate? One cultivates by adverting, by knowing, by seeing, by reviewing, by determining with the mind, by being resolved through faith, by exerting energy, by establishing mindfulness, by composing the mind, by discerning with wisdom, by directly knowing what is to be directly known, by fully understanding what is to be fully understood, by abandoning what is to be abandoned, by developing what is to be developed, and by realizing what is to be realized. In this way, one cultivates.

Bhāvetīti kathaṃ bhāveti? Āvajjanto bhāveti, jānanto bhāveti, passanto bhāveti, paccavekkhanto bhāveti, cittaṃ adhiṭṭhahanto bhāveti, saddhāya adhimuccanto bhāveti, vīriyaṃ paggaṇhanto bhāveti, satiṃ upaṭṭhāpento bhāveti, cittaṃ samādahanto bhāveti, paññāya pajānanto bhāveti, abhiññeyyaṃ abhijānanto bhāveti, pariññeyyaṃ parijānanto bhāveti, pahātabbaṃ pajahanto bhāveti, bhāvetabbaṃ bhāvento bhāveti, sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikaronto bhāveti – evaṃ bhāveti.

Regarding 'develops', how does one develop? One develops by adverting, by knowing, by seeing, by reviewing, by determining with the mind, by being resolved through faith, by exerting energy, by establishing mindfulness, by composing the mind, by discerning with wisdom, by directly knowing what is to be directly known, by fully understanding what is to be fully understood, by abandoning what is to be abandoned, by developing what is to be developed, and by realizing what is to be realized. In this way, one develops.

Bahulīkarotīti kathaṃ bahulīkaroti? Āvajjanto bahulīkaroti, jānanto bahulīkaroti, passanto bahulīkaroti, paccavekkhanto bahulīkaroti, cittaṃ adhiṭṭhahanto bahulīkaroti, saddhāya adhimuccanto bahulīkaroti, vīriyaṃ paggaṇhanto bahulīkaroti, satiṃ upaṭṭhāpento bahulīkaroti, cittaṃ samādahanto bahulīkaroti, paññāya pajānanto bahulīkaroti, abhiññeyyaṃ abhijānanto bahulīkaroti, pariññeyyaṃ parijānanto bahulīkaroti, pahātabbaṃ pajahanto bahulīkaroti, bhāvetabbaṃ bhāvento bahulīkaroti, sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikaronto bahulīkaroti – evaṃ bahulīkaroti.

Regarding 'makes much of', how does one make much of? One makes much of by adverting, by knowing, by seeing, by reviewing, by determining with the mind, by being resolved through faith, by exerting energy, by establishing mindfulness, by composing the mind, by discerning with wisdom, by directly knowing what is to be directly known, by fully understanding what is to be fully understood, by abandoning what is to be abandoned, by developing what is to be developed, and by realizing what is to be realized. In this way, one makes much of.

Tassa taṃ maggaṃ āsevato bhāvayato bahulīkaroto saññojanāni pahīyanti [T 1.0436] anusayā byantīhontīti kathaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti? Sotāpattimaggena, sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso – imāni tīṇi saññojanāni pahīyanti; diṭṭhānusayo, vicikicchānusayo – ime dve anusayā byantīhonti. Sakadāgāmimaggena oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgasaññojanaṃ, paṭighasaññojanaṃ – imāni dve saññojanāni pahīyanti; oḷāriko kāmarāgānusayo, paṭighānusayo – ime dve anusayā byantīhonti. Anāgāmimaggena anusahagataṃ kāmarāgasaññojanaṃ, paṭighasaññojanaṃ [P 2.0095] – imāni dve saññojanāni pahīyanti; anusahagato kāmarāgānusayo, paṭighānusayo – ime dve anusayā byantīhonti. Arahattamaggena rūparāgo, arūparāgo, māno, uddhaccaṃ, avijjā – imāni pañca saññojanāni pahīyanti; mānānusayo, bhavarāgānusayo[M 0.0286], avijjānusayo – ime tayo anusayā byantīhonti. Evaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.

For one who cultivates, develops, and makes much of that path, the fetters are abandoned and the underlying tendencies are brought to an end. How are the fetters abandoned and the underlying tendencies brought to an end? By the path of stream-entry, these three fetters are abandoned: identity view, doubt, and clinging to precepts and observances; these two underlying tendencies are brought to an end: the underlying tendency to views and the underlying tendency to doubt. By the path of the once-returner, these two fetters are abandoned: the gross fetter of sensual lust and the fetter of ill will; these two underlying tendencies are brought to an end: the gross underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to ill will. By the path of the non-returner, these two fetters are abandoned: the subtle fetter of sensual lust and the fetter of ill will; these two underlying tendencies are brought to an end: the subtle underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to ill will. By the path of arahantship, these five fetters are abandoned: lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance; these three underlying tendencies are brought to an end: the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to craving for existence, and the underlying tendency to ignorance. It is in this way that the fetters are abandoned and the underlying tendencies are brought to an end.

3. Abyāpādavasena [V 0.0276] cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi…pe… ālokasaññāvasena cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi…pe… paṭinissaggānupassī assāsavasena paṭinissaggānupassī passāsavasena cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi. Tattha jāte dhamme aniccato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā, dukkhato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā, anattato [T 1.0437] anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā. Iti paṭhamaṃ samatho, pacchā vipassanā. Tena vuccati – “samathapubbaṅgamaṃ vipassanaṃ bhāvetī”ti. Bhāvetīti catasso bhāvanā – tattha jātānaṃ dhammānaṃ anativattanaṭṭhena bhāvanā, indriyānaṃ ekarasaṭṭhena bhāvanā, tadupagavīriyavāhanaṭṭhena bhāvanā, āsevanaṭṭhena bhāvanā.

3. By way of non-ill will, one-pointedness of mind and non-distraction is concentration… and so on… by way of the perception of light, one-pointedness of mind and non-distraction is concentration… and so on… by way of the in-breath of one who contemplates relinquishment, and by way of the out-breath of one who contemplates relinquishment, one-pointedness of mind and non-distraction is concentration. Therein, insight is in the sense of contemplating arisen phenomena as impermanent; insight is in the sense of contemplating them as suffering; insight is in the sense of contemplating them as non-self. Thus, serenity is first, insight afterwards. Therefore it is said: ‘One develops insight preceded by serenity.’ Regarding ‘develops,’ there are four kinds of development: development in the sense of not overstepping the phenomena that have arisen therein; development in the sense of the faculties having a single function; development in the sense of applying the energy that leads to it; and development in the sense of cultivation.

Maggo sañjāyatīti kathaṃ maggo sañjāyati? Dassanaṭṭhena sammādiṭṭhi maggo sañjāyati, abhiniropanaṭṭhena sammāsaṅkappo maggo sañjāyati…pe… avikkhepaṭṭhena sammāsamādhi maggo sañjāyati. Evaṃ maggo sañjāyati.

‘The path is known’—how is the path known? In the sense of seeing, Right View is known as the path. In the sense of applying the mind, Right Intention is known as the path… and so on… In the sense of non-distraction, Right Concentration is known as the path. In this way is the path known.

So taṃ maggaṃ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti āsevatīti kathaṃ āsevati? Āvajjanto āsevati…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikaronto āsevati, evaṃ āsevati. Bhāvetīti kathaṃ bhāveti? Āvajjanto bhāveti, jānanto bhāveti…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikaronto bhāveti, evaṃ bhāveti. Bahulīkarotīti kathaṃ bahulīkaroti? Āvajjanto bahulīkaroti, jānanto bahulīkaroti…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikaronto bahulīkaroti, evaṃ bahulīkaroti.

He frequents, develops, and makes much of that path. How does he frequent it? By adverting, he frequents it… and so on… by realizing what is to be realized, he frequents it—thus he frequents it. How does he develop it? By adverting, he develops it; by knowing, he develops it… and so on… by realizing what is to be realized, he develops it—thus he develops it. How does he make much of it? By adverting, he makes much of it; by knowing, he makes much of it… and so on… by realizing what is to be realized, he makes much of it—thus he makes much of it.

Tassa taṃ maggaṃ āsevato bhāvayato bahulīkaroto saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhontīti kathaṃ saññojanā pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti? Sotāpattimaggena [T 1.0438][P 2.0096] sakkāyadiṭṭhi vicikicchā sīlabbataparāmāso – imāni tīṇi saññojanāni pahīyanti; diṭṭhānusayo, vicikicchānusayo – ime dve anusayā byantīhonti. Sakadāgāmimaggena oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgasaññojanaṃ, paṭighasaññojanaṃ – imāni dve saññojanāni pahīyanti; oḷāriko kāmarāgānusayo paṭighānusayo [M 0.0287] – ime dve anusayā byantīhonti. Anāgāmimaggena anusahagataṃ kāmarāgasaññojanaṃ, paṭighasaññojanaṃ – imāni dve saññojanāni pahīyanti; anusahagato kāmarāgānusayo, paṭighānusayo – ime dve anusayā byantīhonti. Arahattamaggena rūparāgo, arūparāgo, māno, uddhaccaṃ, avijjā – imāni pañca saññojanāni pahīyanti; mānānusayo, bhavarāgānusayo, avijjānusayo – ime tayo anusayā [V 0.0277] byantīhonti. Evaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti. Evaṃ samathapubbaṅgamaṃ vipassanaṃ bhāveti.

For one who frequents, develops, and makes much of that path, the fetters are abandoned and the underlying tendencies come to an end. How are the fetters abandoned and the underlying tendencies come to an end? By the path of stream-entry, these three fetters are abandoned: identity view, doubt, and adherence to rules and observances. These two underlying tendencies come to an end: the underlying tendency to views and the underlying tendency to doubt. By the path of the once-returner, the coarse fetter of sensual lust and the fetter of ill will are abandoned; the coarse underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to ill will come to an end. By the path of the non-returner, the subtle fetter of sensual lust and the fetter of ill will are abandoned; the subtle underlying tendency to sensual lust and the underlying tendency to ill will come to an end. By the path of arahantship, these five fetters are abandoned: lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance. These three underlying tendencies come to an end: the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to lust for existence, and the underlying tendency to ignorance. Thus the fetters are abandoned and the underlying tendencies come to an end. In this way, one develops insight preceded by serenity.

4. Kathaṃ vipassanāpubbaṅgamaṃ samathaṃ bhāveti? Aniccato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā, dukkhato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā, anattato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā. Tattha jātānaṃ dhammānañca vosaggārammaṇatā vossaggārammaṇatā (syā. ka.) cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo. Samādhi iti paṭhamaṃ vipassanā, pacchā samatho. Tena vuccati – “vipassanāpubbaṅgamaṃ samathaṃ bhāvetī”ti. Bhāvetīti [T 1.0439] catasso bhāvanā – āsevanaṭṭhena bhāvanā…pe… maggo sañjāyatīti kathaṃ maggo sañjāyati…pe… evaṃ maggo sañjāyati. Evaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.

4. How does one develop serenity preceded by insight? Insight is in the sense of repeatedly contemplating as impermanent; insight is in the sense of repeatedly contemplating as suffering; insight is in the sense of repeatedly contemplating as non-self. The one-pointedness and non-distraction of the mind, which has as its object the relinquishment of the phenomena that have arisen therein, is concentration. Thus, first insight, then serenity. Therefore it is said: “One develops serenity preceded by insight.” In the word “develops,” there are four kinds of development: development in the sense of frequenting… The path arises. How does the path arise? … Thus the path arises. In this way, the fetters are abandoned and the underlying tendencies come to an end.

Rūpaṃ aniccato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā, rūpaṃ dukkhato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā, rūpaṃ anattato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā. Tattha jātānaṃ dhammānañca vosaggārammaṇatā cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi. Iti paṭhamaṃ vipassanā, pacchā samatho. Tena vuccati – “vipassanāpubbaṅgamaṃ samathaṃ bhāvetī”ti. Bhāvetīti catasso bhāvanā – āsevanaṭṭhena bhāvanā…pe… maggo sañjāyatīti kathaṃ maggo sañjāyati…pe… evaṃ maggo sañjāyati. Evaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.

Insight is in the sense of repeatedly contemplating form as impermanent; insight is in the sense of repeatedly contemplating form as suffering; insight is in the sense of repeatedly contemplating form as non-self. Therein, the one-pointedness and non-distraction of the mind, which has as its object the relinquishment of the phenomena that have arisen, is concentration. Thus, first insight, then serenity. Therefore it is said: “He develops serenity preceded by insight.” In the word ‘develops,’ there are four kinds of development: development in the sense of repeated practice… The path arises. How does the path arise? … Thus the path arises. In this way the fetters are abandoned, and the underlying tendencies come to an end.

Vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ [P 2.0097]… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ… cakkhuṃ…pe… jarāmaraṇaṃ aniccato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā, jarāmaraṇaṃ dukkhato…pe… anattato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā. Tattha jātānaṃ dhammānañca vosaggārammaṇatā cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi. Iti paṭhamaṃ vipassanā, pacchā samatho. Tena vuccati – “vipassanāpubbaṅgamaṃ samathaṃ bhāvetī”ti. Bhāvetīti catasso bhāvanā – āsevanaṭṭhena bhāvanā…pe… maggo sañjāyatīti kathaṃ [M 0.0288] maggo sañjāyati…pe… evaṃ maggo sañjāyati. Evaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti. Evaṃ vipassanāpubbaṅgamaṃ samathaṃ [T 1.0440] bhāveti.

Insight is in the sense of repeatedly contemplating feeling… perception… formations… consciousness… the eye… up to… aging and death as impermanent; insight is in the sense of repeatedly contemplating aging and death as suffering… as non-self. Therein, the one-pointedness and non-distraction of the mind, which has as its object the relinquishment of the phenomena that have arisen, is concentration. Thus, first insight, then serenity. Therefore it is said: “He develops serenity preceded by insight.” In the word ‘develops,’ there are four kinds of development: development in the sense of repeated practice… The path arises. How does the path arise? … Thus the path arises. In this way the fetters are abandoned, and the underlying tendencies come to an end. Thus he develops serenity preceded by insight.

5. Kathaṃ samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Soḷasahi ākārehi samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti. Ārammaṇaṭṭhena gocaraṭṭhena pahānaṭṭhena pariccāgaṭṭhena vuṭṭhānaṭṭhena vivaṭṭanaṭṭhena santaṭṭhena paṇītaṭṭhena vimuttaṭṭhena anāsavaṭṭhena taraṇaṭṭhena animittaṭṭhena appaṇihitaṭṭhena suññataṭṭhena ekarasaṭṭhena anativattanaṭṭhena yuganaddhaṭṭhena.

5. How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together? One develops serenity and insight yoked together in sixteen aspects: in the sense of object, domain, abandoning, relinquishing, emergence, turning away, peacefulness, the sublime, liberation, taintlessness, crossing over, the signless, emptiness, single essence, not overstepping, and being yoked together.

Kathaṃ [V 0.0278] ārammaṇaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccaṃ pajahato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi nirodhārammaṇo, avijjaṃ pajahato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā nirodhārammaṇā. Iti ārammaṇaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “ārammaṇaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti. Bhāvetīti catasso bhāvanā – āsevanaṭṭhena bhāvanā…pe… maggo sañjāyatīti kathaṃ maggo sañjāyati…pe… evaṃ maggo sañjāyati. Evaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti. Evaṃ ārammaṇaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the aspect of object? For one abandoning restlessness, the one-pointedness and non-distraction of mind—concentration—has cessation as its object. For one abandoning ignorance, insight, in the sense of contemplation, has cessation as its object. Thus, in the aspect of object, serenity and insight are of a single essence, are yoked together, and do not overstep one another. Therefore it is said: “One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the aspect of object.” “Develops” refers to the four kinds of development: development in the sense of frequenting… The path arises. How does the path arise? … Thus the path arises. In this way the fetters are abandoned and the underlying tendencies are brought to an end. Thus one develops serenity and insight yoked together in the aspect of object.

Kathaṃ gocaraṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccaṃ pajahato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi nirodhagocaro, avijjaṃ pajahato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā nirodhagocarā. Iti gocaraṭṭhena [T 1.0441] samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti[P 2.0098]. Tena vuccati – “gocaraṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the aspect of domain? For one abandoning restlessness, the one-pointedness and non-distraction of mind—concentration—has cessation as its domain. For one abandoning ignorance, insight, in the sense of contemplation, has cessation as its domain. Thus, in the aspect of domain, serenity and insight are of a single essence, are yoked together, and do not overstep one another. Therefore it is said: “One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the aspect of domain.”

Kathaṃ pahānaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccasahagatakilese ca khandhe ca pajahato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi nirodhagocaro, avijjāsahagatakilese ca khandhe ca pajahato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā nirodhagocarā. Iti pahānaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “pahānaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the aspect of abandoning? For one abandoning the defilements and aggregates that accompany restlessness, the one-pointedness and non-distraction of mind—concentration—has cessation as its domain. For one abandoning the defilements and aggregates that accompany ignorance, insight, in the sense of contemplation, has cessation as its domain. Thus, in the aspect of abandoning, serenity and insight are of a single essence, are yoked together, and do not overstep one another. Therefore it is said: “One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the aspect of abandoning.”

Kathaṃ pariccāgaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccasahagatakilese ca khandhe ca pariccajato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi nirodhagocaro, avijjāsahagatakilese ca khandhe ca pariccajato anupassanaṭṭhena [M 0.0289] vipassanā nirodhagocarā. Iti pariccāgaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “pariccāgaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of relinquishing? For one who relinquishes the defilements and aggregates that accompany restlessness, the one-pointedness and non-distraction of mind—concentration—has cessation as its domain. For one who relinquishes the defilements and aggregates that accompany ignorance, insight in the sense of contemplation has cessation as its domain. Thus, in the sense of relinquishing, serenity and insight are of a single function, are yoked together, and do not overstep one another. Therefore it is said: “One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of relinquishing.”

Kathaṃ vuṭṭhānaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccasahagatakilesehi ca khandhehi ca vuṭṭhahato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi nirodhagocaro, avijjāsahagatakilesehi ca khandhehi ca [T 1.0442] vuṭṭhahato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā nirodhagocarā. Iti vuṭṭhānaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “vuṭṭhānaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of emergence? For one who emerges from the defilements and aggregates that accompany restlessness, the one-pointedness and non-distraction of mind—concentration—has cessation as its domain. For one who emerges from the defilements and aggregates that accompany ignorance, insight in the sense of contemplation has cessation as its domain. Thus, in the sense of emergence, serenity and insight are of a single function, are yoked together, and do not overstep one another. Therefore it is said: “One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of emergence.”

Kathaṃ [V 0.0279] vivaṭṭanaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccasahagatakilesehi ca khandhehi ca vivaṭṭato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi nirodhagocaro, avijjāsahagatakilesehi ca khandhehi ca vivaṭṭato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā nirodhagocarā. Iti vivaṭṭanaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “vivaṭṭanaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of turning away? For one who turns away from the defilements and aggregates that accompany restlessness, the one-pointedness and non-distraction of mind—concentration—has cessation as its domain. For one who turns away from the defilements and aggregates that accompany ignorance, insight in the sense of contemplation has cessation as its domain. Thus, in the sense of turning away, serenity and insight are of a single function, are yoked together, and do not overstep one another. Therefore it is said: “One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of turning away.”

Kathaṃ santaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccaṃ pajahato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi santo honti nirodhagocaro, avijjaṃ pajahato [P 2.0099] anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā santā hoti nirodhagocarā. Iti santaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “santaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of peace? For one who abandons restlessness, the mind’s unification and non-distraction—concentration—becomes peaceful, with cessation as its resort. For one who abandons ignorance, insight in the sense of repeated contemplation becomes peaceful, with cessation as its resort. Thus, in the sense of peace, serenity and insight become of a single function, become yoked together, and do not overstep one another. Therefore it is said: ‘One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of peace.’

Kathaṃ paṇītaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccaṃ pajahato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi paṇīto hoti nirodhagocaro, avijjaṃ pajahato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā paṇītā hoti nirodhagocarā[T 1.0443]. Iti paṇītaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “paṇītaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of the sublime? For one who abandons restlessness, the mind’s unification and non-distraction—concentration—becomes sublime, with cessation as its resort. For one who abandons ignorance, insight in the sense of repeated contemplation becomes sublime, with cessation as its resort. Thus, in the sense of the sublime, serenity and insight become of a single function, become yoked together, and do not overstep one another. Therefore it is said: ‘One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of the sublime.’

Kathaṃ vimuttaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccaṃ pajahato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi kāmāsavā vimutto hoti nirodhagocaro, avijjaṃ pajahato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā avijjāsavā vimuttā [M 0.0290] hoti nirodhagocarā. Iti rāgavirāgā cetovimutti avijjāvirāgā paññā vimuttaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “vimuttaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of liberation? For one who abandons restlessness, the mind’s unification and non-distraction—concentration—is liberated from the taint of sensual desire, with cessation as its resort. For one who abandons ignorance, insight in the sense of repeated contemplation is liberated from the taint of ignorance, with cessation as its resort. Thus, in the sense of liberation—liberation of mind through dispassion for lust and liberation by wisdom through dispassion for ignorance—serenity and insight become of a single function, become yoked together, and do not overstep one another. Therefore it is said: ‘One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of liberation.’

Kathaṃ anāsavaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccaṃ pajahato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi kāmāsavena anāsavo hoti nirodhagocaro, avijjaṃ pajahato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā avijjāsavena anāsavā hoti nirodhagocarā. Iti anāsavaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “anāsavaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of taintlessness? For one who abandons restlessness, the mind’s unification, non-distraction—concentration—is free from the taint of sensual desire, with cessation as its object. For one who abandons ignorance, insight in the sense of contemplation is free from the taint of ignorance, with cessation as its object. Thus, in the sense of taintlessness, serenity and insight become of a single function, yoked together, not overstepping one another. Therefore it is said: ‘One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of taintlessness.’

Kathaṃ [V 0.0280] taraṇaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccasahagatakilese ca khandhe ca tarato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi nirodhagocaro, avijjāsahagatakilese ca khandhe ca tarato anupassanaṭṭhena [T 1.0444] vipassanā nirodhagocarā. Iti taraṇaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “taraṇaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of crossing over? For one who crosses over the defilements and aggregates accompanied by restlessness, the mind’s unification, non-distraction—concentration—has cessation as its object. For one who crosses over the defilements and aggregates accompanied by ignorance, insight in the sense of contemplation has cessation as its object. Thus, in the sense of crossing over, serenity and insight become of a single function, yoked together, not overstepping one another. Therefore it is said: ‘One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of crossing over.’

Kathaṃ animittaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ [P 2.0100] bhāveti? Uddhaccaṃ pajahato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi sabbanimittehi animitto hoti nirodhagocaro, avijjaṃ pajahato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā sabbanimittehi animittā hoti nirodhagocarā. Iti animittaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “animittaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of the signless? For one who abandons restlessness, the mind’s unification, non-distraction—concentration—becomes signless in regard to all signs, with cessation as its object. For one who abandons ignorance, insight in the sense of contemplation becomes signless in regard to all signs, with cessation as its object. Thus, in the sense of the signless, serenity and insight become of a single function, yoked together, not overstepping one another. Therefore it is said: ‘One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of the signless.’

Kathaṃ appaṇihitaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccaṃ pajahato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi sabbapaṇidhīhi appaṇihito hoti nirodhagocaro, avijjaṃ pajahato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā sabbapaṇidhīhi appaṇihitā hoti nirodhagocarā. Iti appaṇihitaṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “appaṇihitaṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of the desireless? For one who abandons restlessness, the mind’s one-pointedness, its non-distraction—concentration—is desireless with regard to all desires, having cessation as its resort. For one who abandons ignorance, insight in the sense of repeated contemplation is desireless with regard to all desires, having cessation as its resort. Thus, in the sense of the desireless, serenity and insight are of a single function, are yoked together, and do not overstep one another. Therefore it is said: ‘One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of the desireless.’

Kathaṃ [M 0.0291] suññataṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti? Uddhaccaṃ pajahato cittassa ekaggatā avikkhepo samādhi sabbābhinivesehi suñño hoti nirodhagocaro, avijjaṃ pajahato anupassanaṭṭhena vipassanā [T 1.0445] sabbābhinivesehi suññā hoti nirodhagocarā. Iti suññataṭṭhena samathavipassanā ekarasā honti, yuganaddhā honti, aññamaññaṃ nātivattantīti. Tena vuccati – “suññataṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāvetī”ti. Bhāvetīti catasso bhāvanā – āsevanaṭṭhena bhāvanā…pe… maggo sañjāyatīti kathaṃ maggo sañjāyati…pe… evaṃ maggo sañjāyati. Evaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti. Evaṃ suññataṭṭhena samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti. Imehi soḷasahi ākārehi samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti, evaṃ samathavipassanaṃ yuganaddhaṃ bhāveti.

How does one develop serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of emptiness? For one who abandons restlessness, the mind’s one-pointedness, its non-distraction—concentration—is empty of all adherences, having cessation as its resort. For one who abandons ignorance, insight in the sense of repeated contemplation is empty of all adherences, having cessation as its resort. Thus, in the sense of emptiness, serenity and insight are of a single function, are yoked together, and do not overstep one another. Therefore it is said: ‘One develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of emptiness.’ In the word ‘develops,’ there are four kinds of development—development in the sense of cultivation… The path arises. How does the path arise? … Thus the path arises. In this way, the fetters are abandoned, and the underlying tendencies cease. Thus one develops serenity and insight yoked together in the sense of emptiness. One develops serenity and insight yoked together by these sixteen aspects. Thus one develops serenity and insight yoked together.

Suttantaniddeso.

The Exposition of the Suttanta is finished.

2. Dhammuddhaccavāraniddeso

2. The Exposition of the Section on Restlessness regarding Dhammas

6. Kathaṃ [V 0.0281] dhammuddhaccaviggahitaṃ mānasaṃ hoti? Aniccato manasikaroto obhāso uppajjati, obhāso [P 2.0101] dhammoti obhāsaṃ āvajjati, tato vikkhepo uddhaccaṃ. Tena uddhaccena viggahitamānaso aniccato upaṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, dukkhato upaṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, anattato upaṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Tena vuccati – “dhammuddhaccaviggahitamānaso hoti so samayo, yaṃ taṃ cittaṃ ajjhattameva santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati[T 1.0446]. Tassa maggo sañjāyatī”ti kathaṃ maggo sañjāyati…pe… evaṃ maggo sañjāyati, evaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.

6. How is the mind seized by restlessness concerning phenomena? When one attends by way of impermanence, an illumination arises. One attends to the illumination, [thinking,] 'Illumination is the Dhamma'; from that, distraction, which is restlessness, arises. With a mind seized by that restlessness, one does not discern as it truly is the manifestation by way of impermanence, one does not discern as it truly is the manifestation by way of suffering, one does not discern as it truly is the manifestation by way of not-self. Therefore it is said: 'That is the occasion when the mind is seized by restlessness concerning phenomena. When that mind becomes internally steady, settled, unified, and concentrated, the path is generated for him.' How is the path generated? …pe… Thus the path is generated, thus the fetters are abandoned, and the underlying tendencies are brought to an end.

Aniccato manasikaroto ñāṇaṃ uppajjati, pīti uppajjati, passaddhi uppajjati, sukhaṃ uppajjati, adhimokkho uppajjati, paggaho uppajjati, upaṭṭhānaṃ uppajjati, upekkhā uppajjati, nikanti uppajjati, ‘nikanti dhammo’ti nikantiṃ āvajjati. Tato vikkhepo uddhaccaṃ. Tena uddhaccena viggahitamānaso aniccato upaṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, dukkhato upaṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, anattato upaṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Tena vuccati – “dhammuddhaccaviggahitamānaso [M 0.0292] hoti so samayo, yaṃ taṃ cittaṃ ajjhattameva santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Tassa maggo sañjāyatī”ti. Kathaṃ maggo sañjāyati…pe… evaṃ maggo sañjāyati, evaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.

When one attends by way of impermanence, knowledge arises, rapture arises, tranquility arises, happiness arises, resolve arises, exertion arises, mindfulness arises, equanimity arises, and craving (nikanti) arises. One attends to craving (nikanti), [thinking,] 'Craving (nikanti) is the Dhamma.' From that, distraction, which is restlessness, arises. With a mind seized by that restlessness, one does not discern as it truly is the manifestation by way of impermanence, one does not discern as it truly is the manifestation by way of suffering, one does not discern as it truly is the manifestation by way of not-self. Therefore it is said: 'That is the occasion when the mind is seized by restlessness concerning phenomena. When that mind becomes internally steady, settled, unified, and concentrated, the path is generated for him.' How is the path generated? …pe… Thus the path is generated, thus the fetters are abandoned, and the underlying tendencies are brought to an end.

Dukkhato manasikaroto…pe… anattato manasikaroto obhāso uppajjati…pe… ñāṇaṃ uppajjati, pīti uppajjati, passaddhi uppajjati, sukhaṃ uppajjati, adhimokkho uppajjati, paggaho uppajjati, upaṭṭhānaṃ uppajjati, upekkhā uppajjati, nikanti uppajjati, ‘nikanti dhammo’ti nikantiṃ āvajjati. Tato vikkhepo uddhaccaṃ. Tena uddhaccena viggahitamānaso [T 1.0447] anattato upaṭṭhānaṃ, aniccato upaṭṭhānaṃ, dukkhato upaṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti[P 2.0102]. Tena vuccati – “dhammuddhaccaviggahitamānaso…pe… evaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti”.

To one who attends as suffering …pe… to one who attends as not-self, an illumination arises …pe… knowledge arises, rapture arises, tranquility arises, happiness arises, resolve arises, exertion arises, establishment arises, equanimity arises, and delight arises. One reflects on delight, thinking, 'Delight is the Dhamma.' From that, distraction is restlessness. With a mind seized by that restlessness, one does not know as it really is the establishment as not-self, the establishment as impermanence, and the establishment as suffering. Therefore it is said: 'one with a mind seized by restlessness concerning phenomena …pe… thus the fetters are abandoned, and the underlying tendencies are brought to an end.'

Rūpaṃ aniccato manasikaroto…pe… rūpaṃ dukkhato manasikaroto… rūpaṃ anattato manasikaroto… vedanaṃ…pe… saññaṃ… saṅkhāre… viññāṇaṃ… cakkhuṃ…pe… jarāmaraṇaṃ aniccato [V 0.0282] manasikaroto…pe… jarāmaraṇaṃ dukkhato manasikaroto, jarāmaraṇaṃ anattato manasikaroto obhāso uppajjati…pe… ñāṇaṃ uppajjati, pīti uppajjati, passaddhi uppajjati, sukhaṃ uppajjati, adhimokkho uppajjati, paggaho uppajjati, upaṭṭhānaṃ uppajjati, upekkhā uppajjati, nikanti uppajjati, ‘nikanti dhammo’ti nikantiṃ āvajjati. Tato vikkhepo uddhaccaṃ. Tena uddhaccena viggahitamānaso. Jarāmaraṇaṃ anattato upaṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Jarāmaraṇaṃ aniccato upaṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, jarāmaraṇaṃ dukkhato upaṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. Tena vuccati – “dhammuddhaccaviggahitamānaso hoti. So samayo, yaṃ taṃ cittaṃ ajjhattameva santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati. Tassa maggo sañjāyatī”ti. Kathaṃ maggo sañjāyati…pe… evaṃ maggo sañjāyati. Evaṃ saññojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti. Evaṃ dhammuddhaccaviggahitaṃ [T 1.0448] mānasaṃ hoti.

To one who attends to form as impermanent... (etc.)... to one who attends to form as suffering... to one who attends to form as not-self... feeling... (etc.)... perception... formations... consciousness... the eye... (etc.)... to one who attends to aging-and-death as impermanent... (etc.)... to one who attends to aging-and-death as suffering, to one who attends to aging-and-death as not-self, an illumination arises... (etc.)... knowledge arises, rapture arises, tranquility arises, happiness arises, resolve arises, exertion arises, establishment arises, equanimity arises, and delight arises. He attends to delight, thinking, 'Delight is the Dhamma.' From that, distraction, which is restlessness, arises. With a mind seized by that restlessness, he does not know as it really is the establishment of aging-and-death as not-self. He does not know as it really is the establishment of aging-and-death as impermanent. He does not know as it really is the establishment of aging-and-death as suffering. Therefore, it is said: 'He becomes one with a mind seized by restlessness concerning phenomena.' That is the occasion when that mind becomes internally steady, settles down, becomes unified, and is concentrated. For him, the path is generated. How is the path generated? ... (etc.) ... Thus the path is generated. Thus the fetters are abandoned, and the underlying tendencies are brought to an end. Thus the mind becomes seized by restlessness concerning phenomena.

7.

7.

Obhāse ceva ñāṇe ca, pītiyā ca vikampati;

Passaddhiyā sukhe ceva, yehi cittaṃ pavedhati.

In illumination and in knowledge, and in rapture, the mind wavers; in tranquility and in happiness, by which the mind is shaken.

Adhimokkhe [M 0.0293] ca paggāhe, upaṭṭhāne ca kampati;

Upekkhāvajjanāya ceva, upekkhāya ca nikantiyā.

In resolve and in exertion, and in establishment, it wavers; and in adverting to equanimity, in equanimity, and in delight.

Imāni dasa ṭhānāni, paññā yassa pariccitā;

Dhammuddhaccakusalo hoti, na ca sammoha gacchati.

He whose wisdom has comprehended these ten items becomes skilled in restlessness concerning phenomena and does not fall into delusion.

Vikkhipati ceva kilissati ca, cavati cittabhāvanā;

Vikkhipati [P 2.0103] na kilissati, bhāvanā parihāyati.

When the mind is distracted and defiled, the mental development falls away. When the mind is distracted but not defiled, the development diminishes.

Vikkhipati na kilissati, bhāvanā na parihāyati;

Na ca vikkhipate cittaṃ na kilissati, na cavati cittabhāvanā.

When the mind is distracted but not defiled, the development does not diminish. And the mind is not distracted and not defiled, and the mental development does not fall away.

Imehi catūhi ṭhānehi cittassa saṅkhepavikkhepaviggahitaṃ saṅkhepaṃ vikkhepaṃ viggahitaṃ (syā.) dasa ṭhāne sampajānātīti.

By these four states, one clearly comprehends in ten instances the mind's being perversely grasped through contraction and distraction.

Yuganaddhakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Yoked is concluded.

2. Saccakathā

2. Discourse on Truth

8. Purimanidānaṃ[V 0.0283]. “Cattārimāni[P 2.0104], bhikkhave saṃ. ni. 5.1090, tathāni avitathāni anaññathāni. Katamāni cattāri? ‘Idaṃ dukkha’nti, bhikkhave, tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathametaṃ[T 1.0449]; ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathametaṃ, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathametaṃ, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathametaṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri tathāni avitathāni anaññathāni”.

8. The introduction is as before. “Bhikkhus, these four things are real, not unreal, not otherwise. What four? ‘This is suffering,’ bhikkhus: this is real, this is not unreal, this is not otherwise. ‘This is the origin of suffering’: this is real, this is not unreal, this is not otherwise. ‘This is the cessation of suffering’: this is real, this is not unreal, this is not otherwise. ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering’: this is real, this is not unreal, this is not otherwise. These, bhikkhus, are the four things that are real, not unreal, not otherwise.”

1. Paṭhamasuttantaniddeso

1. Exposition of the First Sutta

Kathaṃ dukkhaṃ tathaṭṭhena saccaṃ? Cattāro dukkhassa dukkhaṭṭhā tathā avitathā anaññathā. Dukkhassa pīḷanaṭṭho, saṅkhataṭṭho, santāpaṭṭho, vipariṇāmaṭṭho – ime cattāro dukkhassa dukkhaṭṭhā tathā avitathā anaññathā. Evaṃ dukkhaṃ tathaṭṭhena saccaṃ.

How is suffering a truth in the sense of actuality? The four meanings of suffering as suffering are real, not unreal, not otherwise. The meaning of oppression, the meaning of being conditioned, the meaning of torment, and the meaning of change—these four meanings of suffering as suffering are real, not unreal, not otherwise. Thus suffering is a truth in the sense of actuality.

Kathaṃ samudayo tathaṭṭhena saccaṃ? Cattāro samudayassa samudayaṭṭhā tathā avitathā anaññathā. Samudayassa āyūhanaṭṭho, nidānaṭṭho, saṃyogaṭṭho [M 0.0294] palibodhaṭṭho – ime cattāro samudayassa samudayaṭṭhā tathā avitathā anaññathā. Evaṃ samudayo tathaṭṭhena saccaṃ.

How is the origin a truth in the sense of actuality? The four meanings of the origin as origin are real, not unreal, not otherwise. The meaning of accumulation, the meaning of source, the meaning of bondage, and the meaning of impediment—these four meanings of the origin as origin are real, not unreal, not otherwise. Thus the origin is a truth in the sense of actuality.

Kathaṃ nirodho tathaṭṭhena saccaṃ? Cattāro nirodhassa [P 2.0105] nirodhaṭṭhā tathā avitathā anaññathā. Nirodhassa nissaraṇaṭṭho, vivekaṭṭho, asaṅkhataṭṭho, amataṭṭho – ime cattāro nirodhassa nirodhaṭṭhā tathā avitathā anaññathā. Evaṃ nirodho tathaṭṭhena saccaṃ.

How is cessation a truth in the sense of actuality? The four meanings of cessation as cessation are real, not unreal, not otherwise. The meaning of escape, the meaning of seclusion, the meaning of the unconditioned, and the meaning of the deathless—these four meanings of cessation as cessation are real, not unreal, not otherwise. Thus cessation is a truth in the sense of actuality.

Kathaṃ maggo tathaṭṭhena saccaṃ? Cattāro maggassa maggaṭṭhā tathā avitathā anaññathā. Maggassa [V 0.0284] niyyānaṭṭho, hetuṭṭho, dassanaṭṭho, ādhipateyyaṭṭho – ime cattāro maggassa maggaṭṭhā tathā avitathā anaññathā. Evaṃ maggo tathaṭṭhena saccaṃ.

How is the path a truth in the sense of actuality? The four path-meanings of the path are actual, not un-actual, not otherwise. The meaning of deliverance, the meaning of cause, the meaning of seeing, and the meaning of dominance—these four path-meanings of the path are actual, not un-actual, not otherwise. Thus, the path is a truth in the sense of actuality.

9. Katihākārehi [T 1.0450] cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Catūhākārehi cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni. Tathaṭṭhena, anattaṭṭhena, saccaṭṭhena, paṭivedhaṭṭhena – imehi catūhākārehi cattāri saccāni ekasaṅgahitāni. Yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

9. In how many aspects are the four truths penetrated as one? The four truths are penetrated as one in four aspects. In the sense of actuality, in the sense of non-self, in the sense of truth, and in the sense of penetration—by these four aspects the four truths are comprised as one. What is comprised as one is a unity. That unity is penetrated by a single knowledge—thus the four truths are penetrated as one.

Kathaṃ tathaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Catūhākārehi tathaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni. Dukkhassa dukkhaṭṭho tathaṭṭho, samudayassa samudayaṭṭho tathaṭṭho, nirodhassa nirodhaṭṭho tathaṭṭho, maggassa maggaṭṭho tathaṭṭho – imehi catūhākārehi tathaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekasaṅgahitāni. Yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

How, in the sense of actuality, are the four truths penetrated as one? In four aspects, in the sense of actuality, the four truths are penetrated as one. The meaning of suffering as suffering is the sense of actuality; the meaning of the origin as origin is the sense of actuality; the meaning of cessation as cessation is the sense of actuality; the meaning of the path as path is the sense of actuality. By these four aspects, in the sense of actuality, the four truths are comprised as one. What is comprised as one is a unity. That unity is penetrated by a single knowledge—thus the four truths are penetrated as one.

Kathaṃ anattaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Catūhākārehi anattaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni. Dukkhassa dukkhaṭṭho anattaṭṭho, samudayassa samudayaṭṭho anattaṭṭho, nirodhassa nirodhaṭṭho anattaṭṭho, maggassa maggaṭṭho anattaṭṭho – imehi catūhākārehi anattaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekasaṅgahitāni. Yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

How, in the sense of non-self, are the four truths penetrated as one? In four aspects, in the sense of non-self, the four truths are penetrated as one. The meaning of suffering as suffering is the sense of non-self; the meaning of the origin as origin is the sense of non-self; the meaning of cessation as cessation is the sense of non-self; the meaning of the path as path is the sense of non-self. By these four aspects, in the sense of non-self, the four truths are comprised as one. What is comprised as one is a unity. That unity is penetrated by a single knowledge—thus the four truths are penetrated as one.

Kathaṃ saccaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Catūhākārehi saccaṭṭhena [T 1.0451] cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni. Dukkhassa dukkhaṭṭho saccaṭṭho, samudayassa [M 0.0295] samudayaṭṭho saccaṭṭho, nirodhassa nirodhaṭṭho saccaṭṭho, maggassa [P 2.0106] maggaṭṭho saccaṭṭho – imehi catūhākārehi saccaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekasaṅgahitāni. Yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

How, in the sense of truth, are the four truths penetrated as one? In four aspects, in the sense of truth, the four truths are penetrated as one. Of suffering, the meaning of suffering is the meaning of truth; of the origin, the meaning of origin is the meaning of truth; of cessation, the meaning of cessation is the meaning of truth; of the path, the meaning of the path is the meaning of truth. By these four aspects, in the sense of truth, the four truths are comprised as one. That which is comprised as one is oneness. Oneness is penetrated by a single knowledge—thus the four truths are penetrated as one.

Kathaṃ paṭivedhaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Catūhākārehi paṭivedhaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni. Dukkhassa dukkhaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho, samudayassa samudayaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho nirodhassa nirodhaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho, maggassa maggaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho – imehi catūhākārehi paṭivedhaṭṭhena cattāri [V 0.0285] saccāni ekasaṅgahitāni yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

How, in the sense of penetration, are the four truths penetrated as one? In four aspects, in the sense of penetration, the four truths are penetrated as one. Of suffering, the meaning of suffering is the meaning of penetration; of the origin, the meaning of origin is the meaning of penetration; of cessation, the meaning of cessation is the meaning of penetration; of the path, the meaning of the path is the meaning of penetration. By these four aspects, in the sense of penetration, the four truths are comprised as one. That which is comprised as one is oneness. Oneness is penetrated by a single knowledge—thus the four truths are penetrated as one.

10. Katihākārehi cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Yaṃ aniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ, yaṃ dukkhaṃ taṃ aniccaṃ, yaṃ aniccañca dukkhañca taṃ anattā. Yaṃ aniccañca dukkhañca anattā ca taṃ tathaṃ. Yaṃ aniccaṃ ca dukkhañca anattā ca tathañca taṃ saccaṃ. Yaṃ aniccañca dukkhañca anattā ca tathañca saccañca taṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ. Yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

10. In how many aspects are the four truths penetrated as one? That which is impermanent is suffering; that which is suffering is impermanent; that which is impermanent and suffering is non-self. That which is impermanent, suffering, and non-self is real. That which is impermanent, suffering, non-self, and real is truth. That which is impermanent, suffering, non-self, real, and truth is comprised as one. That which is comprised as one is oneness. Oneness is penetrated by a single knowledge—thus the four truths are penetrated as one.

Katihākārehi [T 1.0452] cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Navahākārehi cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni. Tathaṭṭhena, anattaṭṭhena, saccaṭṭhena, paṭivedhaṭṭhena, abhiññaṭṭhena, pariññaṭṭhena, pahānaṭṭhena, bhāvanaṭṭhena, sacchikiriyaṭṭhena – imehi navahākārehi cattāri saccāni ekasaṅgahitāni. Yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

In how many aspects are the four truths penetrated as one? The four truths are penetrated as one in nine aspects. In the sense of actuality, in the sense of not-self, in the sense of truth, in the sense of penetration, in the sense of direct knowledge, in the sense of full understanding, in the sense of abandonment, in the sense of development, and in the sense of realization—by these nine aspects the four truths are comprised as one. What is comprised as one is a unity. That unity is penetrated by a single knowledge—thus the four truths are penetrated as one.

Kathaṃ tathaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Navahākārehi tathaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni. Dukkhassa dukkhaṭṭho tathaṭṭho, samudayassa samudayaṭṭho tathaṭṭho, nirodhassa nirodhaṭṭho tathaṭṭho, maggassa maggaṭṭho tathaṭṭho, abhiññāya abhiññaṭṭho tathaṭṭho, pariññāya pariññaṭṭho tathaṭṭho, pahānassa pahānaṭṭho tathaṭṭho, bhāvanāya bhāvanaṭṭho tathaṭṭho, sacchikiriyāya sacchikiriyaṭṭho tathaṭṭho – imehi navahākārehi tathaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekasaṅgahitāni. Yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

How, in the sense of actuality, are the four truths penetrated as one? In nine aspects, in the sense of actuality, are the four truths penetrated as one. The nature of suffering is the actual nature; the nature of the origin is the actual nature; the nature of cessation is the actual nature; the nature of the path is the actual nature; the nature of direct knowledge is the actual nature; the nature of full understanding is the actual nature; the nature of abandonment is the actual nature; the nature of development is the actual nature; the nature of realization is the actual nature. By these nine aspects, in the sense of actuality, the four truths are comprised as one. What is comprised as one is a unity. That unity is penetrated by a single knowledge—thus the four truths are penetrated as one.

Kathaṃ [P 2.0107][M 0.0296] anattaṭṭhena… saccaṭṭhena… paṭivedhaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Navahākārehi paṭivedhaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni. Dukkhassa dukkhaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho, samudayassa samudayaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho, nirodhassa nirodhaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho, maggassa maggaṭṭho [T 1.0453] paṭivedhaṭṭho, abhiññāya abhiññaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho, pariññāya pariññaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho, pahānassa pahānaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho, bhāvanāya bhāvanaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho, sacchikiriyāya sacchikiriyaṭṭho paṭivedhaṭṭho – imehi navahākārehi paṭivedhaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekasaṅgahitāni. Yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

How, in the sense of non-self, in the sense of truth, and in the sense of penetration, are the four truths penetrated as one? By nine aspects, in the sense of penetration, the four truths are penetrated as one. The meaning of suffering is the meaning of penetration; the meaning of origin is the meaning of penetration; the meaning of cessation is the meaning of penetration; the meaning of the path is the meaning of penetration; the meaning of direct knowledge is the meaning of penetration; the meaning of full understanding is the meaning of penetration; the meaning of abandonment is the meaning of penetration; the meaning of development is the meaning of penetration; and the meaning of realization is the meaning of penetration. By these nine aspects, in the sense of penetration, the four truths are comprised as one. What is comprised as one is a unity. That unity is penetrated by a single knowledge—thus the four truths are penetrated as one.

11. Katihākārehi [V 0.0286] cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Dvādasahi ākārehi cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni. Tathaṭṭhena, anattaṭṭhena, saccaṭṭhena, paṭivedhaṭṭhena, abhijānanaṭṭhena, parijānanaṭṭhena, dhammaṭṭhena, tathaṭṭhena, ñātaṭṭhena, sacchikiriyaṭṭhena, phassanaṭṭhena, abhisamayaṭṭhena – imehi dvādasahi ākārehi cattāri saccāni ekasaṅgahitāni. Yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

11. In how many aspects are the four truths penetrated as one? The four truths are penetrated as one in twelve aspects. In the sense of actuality, in the sense of non-self, in the sense of truth, in the sense of penetration, in the sense of directly knowing, in the sense of full understanding, in the sense of Dhamma, in the sense of actuality, in the sense of the known, in the sense of realization, in the sense of contact, and in the sense of breakthrough—by these twelve aspects the four truths are comprised as one. What is comprised as one is a unity. That unity is penetrated by a single knowledge—thus the four truths are penetrated as one.

Kathaṃ tathaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Soḷasahi ākārehi tathaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni. Dukkhassa pīḷanaṭṭho, saṅkhataṭṭho, santāpaṭṭho, vipariṇāmaṭṭho, tathaṭṭho; samudayassa āyūhanaṭṭho, nidānaṭṭho, saṃyogaṭṭho, palibodhaṭṭho tathaṭṭho; nirodhassa nissaraṇaṭṭho, vivekaṭṭho, asaṅkhataṭṭho, amataṭṭho tathaṭṭho; maggassa niyyānaṭṭho, hetuṭṭho, dassanaṭṭho, ādhipateyyaṭṭho tathaṭṭho – imehi [T 1.0454] soḷasahi ākārehi tathaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekasaṅgahitāni. Yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

How are the four truths penetrated by a single knowledge in the sense of being true? The four truths are penetrated by a single knowledge in the sense of being true by sixteen aspects. For suffering, the meaning of oppression, the meaning of being conditioned, the meaning of torment, and the meaning of change is the meaning of being true. For the origin, the meaning of striving, the meaning of being a source, the meaning of being a bond, and the meaning of being an obstruction is the meaning of being true. For cessation, the meaning of escape, the meaning of seclusion, the meaning of the unconditioned, and the meaning of the deathless is the meaning of being true. For the path, the meaning of outlet, the meaning of being a cause, the meaning of seeing, and the meaning of dominance is the meaning of being true. By these sixteen aspects, the four truths are comprehended as one in the sense of being true. What is comprehended as one is a unity. That unity is penetrated by a single knowledge; thus, the four truths are penetrated by a single knowledge.

Kathaṃ [P 2.0108] anattaṭṭhena…pe… saccaṭṭhena… paṭivedhaṭṭhena… abhijānanaṭṭhena… parijānanaṭṭhena… dhammaṭṭhena… tathaṭṭhena… ñātaṭṭhena… sacchikiriyaṭṭhena… phassanaṭṭhena… abhisamayaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni? Soḷasahi ākārehi abhisamayaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni. Dukkhassa pīḷanaṭṭho, saṅkhataṭṭho, santāpaṭṭho, vipariṇāmaṭṭho, abhisamayaṭṭho; samudayassa āyūhanaṭṭho, nidānaṭṭho, saṃyogaṭṭho, palibodhaṭṭho, abhisamayaṭṭho; nirodhassa nissaraṇaṭṭho[M 0.0297], vivekaṭṭho, asaṅkhataṭṭho, amataṭṭho, abhisamayaṭṭho; maggassa niyyānaṭṭho, hetuṭṭho, dassanaṭṭho, ādhipateyyaṭṭho, abhisamayaṭṭho – imehi soḷasahi ākārehi abhisamayaṭṭhena cattāri saccāni ekasaṅgahitāni. Yaṃ ekasaṅgahitaṃ taṃ ekattaṃ. Ekattaṃ ekena ñāṇena paṭivijjhatīti – cattāri saccāni ekappaṭivedhāni.

How are the four truths penetrated by a single knowledge in the sense of non-self... in the sense of truth... in the sense of penetration... in the sense of direct knowledge... in the sense of full understanding... in the sense of being a phenomenon... in the sense of being true... in the sense of being known... in the sense of realization... in the sense of contact... in the sense of comprehension? The four truths are penetrated by a single knowledge in the sense of comprehension by sixteen aspects. For suffering, the meaning of oppression, the meaning of being conditioned, the meaning of torment, and the meaning of change is the meaning of comprehension. For the origin, the meaning of striving, the meaning of being a source, the meaning of being a bond, and the meaning of being an obstruction is the meaning of comprehension. For cessation, the meaning of escape, the meaning of seclusion, the meaning of the unconditioned, and the meaning of the deathless is the meaning of comprehension. For the path, the meaning of outlet, the meaning of being a cause, the meaning of seeing, and the meaning of dominance is the meaning of comprehension. By these sixteen aspects, the four truths are comprehended as one in the sense of comprehension. What is comprehended as one is a unity. That unity is penetrated by a single knowledge; thus, the four truths are penetrated by a single knowledge.

12. Saccānaṃ kati lakkhaṇāni? Saccānaṃ dve lakkhaṇāni. Saṅkhatalakkhaṇañca, asaṅkhatalakkhaṇañca – saccānaṃ imāni dve lakkhaṇāni.

12. How many characteristics do the truths have? The truths have two characteristics: the characteristic of the conditioned and the characteristic of the unconditioned. These are the two characteristics of the truths.

Saccānaṃ kati lakkhaṇāni? Saccānaṃ cha lakkhaṇāni. Saṅkhatānaṃ saccānaṃ uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitānaṃ aññathattaṃ [T 1.0455] paññāyati asaṅkhatassa saccassa na uppādo paññāyati[V 0.0287], na vayo paññāyati, na ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati – saccānaṃ imāni cha lakkhaṇāni.

How many characteristics do the truths have? The truths have six characteristics. For the conditioned truths, arising is discerned, passing away is discerned, and alteration while persisting is discerned. For the unconditioned truth, arising is not discerned, passing away is not discerned, nor is alteration while persisting discerned. These are the six characteristics of the truths.

Saccānaṃ kati lakkhaṇāni? Saccānaṃ dvādasa lakkhaṇāni. Dukkhasaccassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati; samudayasaccassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati; maggasaccassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati; nirodhasaccassa na uppādo paññāyati, na vayo paññāyati, na ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati – saccānaṃ imāni dvādasa lakkhaṇāni.

How many characteristics do the truths have? The truths have twelve characteristics. For the truth of suffering, arising is discerned, passing away is discerned, and alteration while persisting is discerned. For the truth of origin, arising is discerned, passing away is discerned, and alteration while persisting is discerned. For the truth of the path, arising is discerned, passing away is discerned, and alteration while persisting is discerned. For the truth of cessation, arising is not discerned, passing away is not discerned, nor is alteration while persisting discerned. These are the twelve characteristics of the truths.

Catunnaṃ saccānaṃ kati kusalā, kati akusalā, kati abyākatā? Samudayasaccaṃ akusalaṃ, maggasaccaṃ kusalaṃ[P 2.0109], nirodhasaccaṃ abyākataṃ. Dukkhasaccaṃ siyā kusalaṃ, siyā akusalaṃ, siyā abyākataṃ.

Of the four truths, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, and how many indeterminate? The truth of origin is unwholesome, the truth of the path is wholesome, and the truth of cessation is indeterminate. The truth of suffering may be wholesome, may be unwholesome, or may be indeterminate.

Siyā tīṇi saccāni ekasaccena saṅgahitāni, ekasaccaṃ tīhi saccehi saṅgahitaṃ? Vatthuvasena pariyāyena siyāti. Kathañca siyā? Yaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ akusalaṃ, samudayasaccaṃ akusalaṃ – evaṃ akusalaṭṭhena dve saccāni ekasaccena saṅgahitāni, ekasaccaṃ dvīhi saccehi saṅgahitaṃ. Yaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ kusalaṃ, maggasaccaṃ kusalaṃ – evaṃ kusalaṭṭhena dve saccāni ekasaccena saṅgahitāni[T 1.0456], ekasaccaṃ dvīhi saccehi saṅgahitaṃ. Yaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ abyākataṃ, nirodhasaccaṃ abyākataṃ – evaṃ abyākataṭṭhena dve saccāni ekasaccena saṅgahitāni, ekasaccaṃ dvīhi saccehi saṅgahitaṃ. Evaṃ siyā tīṇi saccāni ekasaccena saṅgahitāni, ekasaccaṃ tīhi saccehi saṅgahitaṃ vatthuvasena pariyāyenāti.

Could it be that three truths are included by one truth, and one truth by three truths? It could be, by way of basis and by way of method. And how could it be? That truth of suffering which is unwholesome, and the truth of the origin which is unwholesome—thus, in the sense of being unwholesome, two truths are included by one truth, and one truth is included by two truths. That truth of suffering which is wholesome, and the truth of the path which is wholesome—thus, in the sense of being wholesome, two truths are included by one truth, and one truth is included by two truths. That truth of suffering which is indeterminate, and the truth of cessation which is indeterminate—thus, in the sense of being indeterminate, two truths are included by one truth, and one truth is included by two truths. Thus, it could be that three truths are included by one truth, and one truth by three truths, by way of basis and by way of method.

2. Dutiyasuttantapāḷi

2. The Pāḷi of the Second Discourse

13. “Pubbe [M 0.0298] me, bhikkhave saṃ. ni. 3.26, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi – ‘ko nu kho rūpassa assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ; ko vedanāya assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ; ko saññāya assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ; ko saṅkhārānaṃ assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ; ko viññāṇassa assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇa’nti? Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘yaṃ kho [V 0.0288] rūpaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ – ayaṃ rūpassa assādo. Yaṃ rūpaṃ aniccaṃ, taṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ – ayaṃ rūpassa ādīnavo. Yo rūpasmiṃ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ – idaṃ rūpassa nissaraṇaṃ. Yaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca…pe… yaṃ saññaṃ paṭicca… yaṃ saṅkhāre paṭicca… yaṃ viññāṇaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ – ayaṃ viññāṇassa assādo. Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ – ayaṃ viññāṇassa ādīnavo. Yo viññāṇasmiṃ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ – idaṃ viññāṇassa nissaraṇaṃ”.

13. “Bhikkhus, before my enlightenment, when I was still an unenlightened Bodhisatta, this thought occurred to me: ‘What now is the gratification in form, what is the danger, what is the escape? What is the gratification in feeling, what is the danger, what is the escape? What is the gratification in perception, what is the danger, what is the escape? What is the gratification in volitional formations, what is the danger, what is the escape? What is the gratification in consciousness, what is the danger, what is the escape?’ Then, Bhikkhus, this thought occurred to me: ‘The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on form—this is the gratification in form. That form is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger in form. The removal of desire and lust, the abandonment of desire and lust for form—this is the escape from form. The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on feeling… in dependence on perception… in dependence on volitional formations… The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on consciousness—this is the gratification in consciousness. That consciousness is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change—this is the danger in consciousness. The removal of desire and lust, the abandonment of desire and lust for consciousness—this is the escape from consciousness.’”

“Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ[T 1.0457], bhikkhave, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ evaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca [P 2.0110] ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññāsiṃ, neva tāvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṃ abhisambuddho paccaññāsiṃ (syā.) saṃ. ni. 3.26 passitabbā yato ca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ evaṃ assādañca assādato ādīnavañca ādīnavato nissaraṇañca nissaraṇato yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, athāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ‘sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti cetovimutti (syā. ka.) saṃ. ni. 3.27 passitabbā. Ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’”ti.

“Bhikkhus, for as long as I did not thoroughly know as they really are the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape in the case of these five aggregates of clinging, for that long, Bhikkhus, I did not claim to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. But when, Bhikkhus, I thoroughly knew as they really are the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, and the escape as escape in the case of these five aggregates of clinging, then, Bhikkhus, I claimed to have fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. And knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘Unshakable is my liberation. This is the final birth. Now there is no more renewed existence.’”

3. Dutiyasuttantaniddeso

3. Exposition of the Second Sutta

14. Yaṃ [M 0.0299] rūpaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ rūpassa assādoti – pahānappaṭivedho samudayasaccaṃ. Yaṃ rūpaṃ aniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, ayaṃ rūpassa ādīnavoti – pariññāpaṭivedho dukkhasaccaṃ. Yo rūpasmiṃ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ rūpassa nissaraṇanti – sacchikiriyāpaṭivedho nirodhasaccaṃ. Yā imesu tīsu ṭhānesu diṭṭhi saṅkappo vācā kammanto ājīvo vāyāmo sati samādhi – bhāvanāpaṭivedho maggasaccaṃ.

14. “Whatever pleasure and joy arise in dependence on form, this is the gratification of form”—this is penetration by abandoning, the truth of the origin. “That form which is impermanent is suffering and subject to change, this is the danger of form”—this is penetration by full understanding, the truth of suffering. “Whatever is the removal of desire and lust for form, the abandonment of desire and lust, this is the escape from form”—this is penetration by realization, the truth of cessation. Whatever in these three instances is right view, right thought, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration—this is penetration by development, the truth of the path.

Yaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca…pe… yaṃ saññaṃ paṭicca… yaṃ saṅkhāre paṭicca… yaṃ viññāṇaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, ayaṃ viññāṇassa [T 1.0458] assādoti – pahānappaṭivedho samudayasaccaṃ. Yaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, ayaṃ viññāṇassa ādīnavoti – pariññāpaṭivedho dukkhasaccaṃ. Yo viññāṇasmiṃ chandarāgavinayo chandarāgappahānaṃ, idaṃ viññāṇassa nissaraṇanti – sacchikiriyāpaṭivedho nirodhasaccaṃ. Yā imesu [V 0.0289] tīsu ṭhānesu diṭṭhi saṅkappo vācā kammanto ājīvo vāyāmo sati samādhi – bhāvanāpaṭivedho maggasaccaṃ.

Whatever pleasure and joy arise in dependence on feeling … on perception … on volitional formations … on consciousness, this is the gratification in consciousness”—this is penetration by abandoning, the truth of the origin. “That consciousness is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, this is the danger in consciousness”—this is penetration by full understanding, the truth of suffering. “The removal of desire and lust, the abandonment of desire and lust for consciousness, this is the escape from consciousness”—this is penetration by realization, the truth of cessation. Whatever view, thought, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, and concentration pertain to these three instances—this is penetration by development, the truth of the path.

15. Saccanti katihākārehi saccaṃ? Esanaṭṭhena[P 2.0111], pariggahaṭṭhena, paṭivedhaṭṭhena. Kathaṃ esanaṭṭhena saccaṃ? Jarāmaraṇaṃ kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavanti – evaṃ esanaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Jarāmaraṇaṃ jātinidānaṃ, jātisamudayaṃ, jātijātikaṃ, jātippabhavanti – evaṃ pariggahaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Jarāmaraṇañca pajānāti, jarāmaraṇasamudayañca pajānāti, jarāmaraṇanirodhañca pajānāti, jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadañca pajānāti – evaṃ paṭivedhaṭṭhena saccaṃ.

15. In how many ways is something a truth? By way of seeking, by way of comprehension, and by way of penetration. How is it a truth by way of seeking? ‘Aging-and-death: what is its condition, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its source?’ Thus it is a truth by way of seeking. ‘Aging-and-death has birth as its condition, birth as its origin, birth as its birth, birth as its source.’ Thus it is a truth by way of comprehension. ‘One discerns aging-and-death, and one discerns the origin of aging-and-death, and one discerns the cessation of aging-and-death, and one discerns the path leading to the cessation of aging-and-death.’ Thus it is a truth by way of penetration.

Jāti kiṃnidānā, kiṃsamudayā, kiṃjātikā, kiṃpabhavāti – evaṃ esanaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Jāti bhavanidānā, bhavasamudayā, bhavajātikā, bhavappabhavāti – evaṃ pariggahaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Jātiñca pajānāti, jātisamudayañca pajānāti, jātinirodhañca pajānāti, jātinirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadañca pajānāti – evaṃ paṭivedhaṭṭhena saccaṃ.

‘Birth: what is its condition, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its source?’ Thus it is a truth by way of seeking. ‘Birth has becoming as its condition, becoming as its origin, becoming as its birth, becoming as its source.’ Thus it is a truth by way of comprehension. ‘One discerns birth, and one discerns the origin of birth, and one discerns the cessation of birth, and one discerns the path leading to the cessation of birth.’ Thus it is a truth by way of penetration.

Bhavo kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavoti – evaṃ esanaṭṭhena saccaṃ[T 1.0459]. Bhavo upādānanidāno, upādānasamudayo, upādānajātiko, upādānappabhavoti – evaṃ pariggahaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Bhavaṃ ca pajānāti, bhavasamudayañca [M 0.0300] pajānāti, bhavanirodhañca pajānāti, bhavanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadañca pajānāti – evaṃ paṭivedhaṭṭhena saccaṃ.

‘What is the cause of becoming, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its source?’ Thus, in the sense of seeking, it is a truth. ‘Becoming has clinging as its cause, clinging as its origin, clinging as its birth, clinging as its source.’ Thus, in the sense of comprehending, it is a truth. ‘One understands becoming, one understands the origin of becoming, one understands the cessation of becoming, and one understands the path leading to the cessation of becoming.’ Thus, in the sense of penetration, it is a truth.

Upādānaṃ kiṃnidānaṃ, kiṃsamudayaṃ, kiṃjātikaṃ, kiṃpabhavanti – evaṃ esanaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Upādānaṃ taṇhānidānaṃ, taṇhāsamudayaṃ, taṇhājātikaṃ, taṇhāpabhavanti – evaṃ pariggahaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Upādānañca pajānāti, upādānasamudayañca pajānāti, upādānanirodhañca pajānāti upādānanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadañca pajānāti – evaṃ paṭivedhaṭṭhena saccaṃ.

‘What is the cause of clinging, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its source?’ Thus, in the sense of seeking, it is a truth. ‘Clinging has craving as its cause, craving as its origin, craving as its birth, craving as its source.’ Thus, in the sense of comprehending, it is a truth. ‘One understands clinging, one understands the origin of clinging, one understands the cessation of clinging, and one understands the path leading to the cessation of clinging.’ Thus, in the sense of penetration, it is a truth.

Taṇhā kiṃnidānā, kiṃsamudayā, kiṃjātikā, kiṃpabhavāti – evaṃ esanaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Taṇhā vedanānidānā, vedanāsamudayā, vedanājātikā, vedanāpabhavāti – evaṃ pariggahaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Taṇhañca pajānāti, taṇhāsamudayañca pajānāti, taṇhānirodhañca pajānāti, taṇhānirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadañca pajānāti – evaṃ paṭivedhaṭṭhena saccaṃ.

‘What is the cause of craving, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its source?’ Thus, in the sense of seeking, it is a truth. ‘Craving has feeling as its cause, feeling as its origin, feeling as its birth, feeling as its source.’ Thus, in the sense of comprehending, it is a truth. ‘One understands craving, one understands the origin of craving, one understands the cessation of craving, and one understands the path leading to the cessation of craving.’ Thus, in the sense of penetration, it is a truth.

Vedanā [V 0.0290][P 2.0112] kiṃnidānā, kiṃsamudayā, kiṃjātikā, kiṃpabhavāti – evaṃ esanaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Vedanā phassanidānā, phassasamudayā, phassajātikā, phassappabhavāti – evaṃ pariggahaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Vedanañca pajānāti, vedanāsamudayañca pajānāti, vedanānirodhañca pajānāti, vedanānirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadañca pajānāti – evaṃ paṭivedhaṭṭhena saccaṃ.

‘What is the cause of feeling, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its source?’ Thus, in the sense of seeking, it is a truth. ‘Feeling has contact as its cause, contact as its origin, contact as its birth, contact as its source.’ Thus, in the sense of comprehending, it is a truth. ‘One understands feeling, one understands the origin of feeling, one understands the cessation of feeling, and one understands the path leading to the cessation of feeling.’ Thus, in the sense of penetration, it is a truth.

Phasso [T 1.0460] kiṃnidāno, kiṃsamudayo, kiṃjātiko, kiṃpabhavoti – evaṃ esanaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Phasso saḷāyatananidāno, saḷāyatanasamudayo, saḷāyatanajātiko, saḷāyatanappabhavoti – evaṃ pariggahaṭṭhena saccaṃ. Phassañca pajānāti, phassasamudayañca pajānāti, phassanirodhañca pajānāti, phassanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadañca pajānāti – evaṃ paṭivedhaṭṭhena saccaṃ.

‘Contact: what is its cause, what is its origin, what is its birth, what is its source?’ Thus, it is a truth in the sense of seeking. ‘Contact has the six sense bases as its cause, the six sense bases as its origin, the six sense bases as its birth, the six sense bases as its source.’ Thus, it is a truth in the sense of comprehension.
